name: Armando
bio: A young Roman whom Wilde knew in April 1900, described to Robert Ross as 'a very smart elegant young Roman Sporus' and, at greater length, as being 'so absurdly like the Apollo Belvedere that I feel always as if I was Winckelmann when I am with him'. Wilde gave him up over the cost of his clothes, took up his best friend instead, and had forgiven him within a fortnight. He survives under a first name only.
bio_note: The best-documented of the Rome cohort: two folios, one carrying a physical description of a kind Wilde wrote about almost nobody else this late. 'Sporus' was Nero's boy-favourite; 'Winckelmann' is Johann Joachim Winckelmann, to whom Pater devoted a chapter of The Renaissance and whose name carries the freight of adult male desire modelled on Greek sculpture. He is the only one of the Roman trio with his own General Index entry ('Armando (boy), 1182, 1184').
